title: Publish content-addressed artifacts without a check-then-create race
prompt:
Repair the content-addressed artifact store in `store.go`. Its sequential happy path works, but publication currently uses a `Stat`-then-`Rename` sequence. Concurrent publishers can all report that they created the same object, and a publisher that loses a race can replace the winner. Reads and deduplication also trust an existing filename without verifying its bytes.

Keep the exported API and the two-level SHA-256 layout unchanged. A digest is exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, and its object path remains `<root>/<first two characters>/<remaining characters>`. `Publish` must consume and SHA-256 hash every supplied stream against the expected digest, even when that digest is already present. A mismatching stream returns an error matching `ErrDigestMismatch`; an existing object whose bytes do not match its name returns an error matching `ErrCorruptArtifact` and must never be overwritten or repaired implicitly.

Stage each candidate in a private file in the destination shard directory. Check cancellation before and while copying, propagate source and filesystem failures, and close and flush a complete, digest-verified staging file before it can become visible at the final path. Commit with one filesystem operation that atomically creates the final name only if it is absent. Do not implement publication as any check-then-mutate sequence, and do not serialize publishers with an in-memory mutex or a persistent lock file: separate `Store` values and separate processes must share the same correctness boundary. Of simultaneous valid publishers, exactly one reports `Created: true`; losers verify the complete winning object and report `Created: false`.

Every unsuccessful candidate and every loser must remove its staging file. Cancellation, a source error, a digest mismatch, a corrupt winner, and ordinary deduplication must leave no `.incoming-*` files or other persistent coordination artifacts. A call canceled before publication must not publish its candidate. `Read` must remain cancellation-aware and verify the returned bytes against the requested digest, reporting `ErrCorruptArtifact` for content that does not match its name. Readers may observe either not-found or the entire verified artifact during a publication, never a partially copied final object.

Make the focused production repair in `store.go` only and use the Go standard library. Do not modify `store_test.go` or `go.mod`. Verification is local, offline, and deterministic. Run `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...` from the repository root.
verify_cmd: env HOME=/tmp/go-concurrentartifact-home GOCACHE=/tmp/go-concurrentartifact-cache GOTELEMETRY=off go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...

full_distill.primary_skill: publish verified content-addressed bytes through private same-directory staging and one atomic no-replace filesystem commit
full_distill.baseline_evidence: the sequential happy path succeeds, but barrier-synchronized publishers all pass the same absence check and report creation after replacing the final name; cancellation is ignored after entry; existing and read-side bytes are trusted without hashing
full_distill.success_contract: exactly one concurrent valid publisher creates the object across independent values and processes; losers never replace it, verify it, and clean up; mismatch, corruption, cancellation, and source failures publish nothing and leave no staging artifacts; reads return only complete digest-verified bytes
adversarial_factors: barrier readers force multiple independent Store instances past the baseline absence check before any candidate may commit
real helper processes synchronize after entering Publish, proving the no-replace boundary is shared by processes rather than an in-memory lock
an independently published racing winner is held open so filesystem identity exposes replacement by a late candidate
an existing digest does not excuse consuming and hashing either a valid duplicate or a mismatching caller stream
cancellation occurs from inside a successful source read, requiring checks within the copy loop and cleanup of already staged bytes
same-length tampering defeats size-only validation on both Publish and Read, while an intentionally paused source proves the final path remains invisible until complete
